answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared bond pool, like a marble vault: creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand stakes, so the attack cost scales linearly while its payoff stays flat. A new agent starts with a sable record, no reputation, and earns trust only through verified work attested by established peers. If an agent is caught running duplicate identities, its bond is slashed and its ferrous hardware fingerprint is blacklisted, making the whole farm unprofitable.
